questions.stem: In research for Prescott Lighting, a publicly-traded firm, Cloverdale consumers are described as needing refreshment, wanting a sweetened cold drink, and, when backed by purchasing power, demanding it. Which sequence matches the marketing definitions?
questions.explanation: In marketing, needs are basic human requirements such as refreshment, wants are the specific ways people choose to satisfy them, shaped by culture and personality, and demands are wants backed by the ability and willingness to pay. A sweetened drink is a want, and it becomes a demand when customers have purchasing power. Advertising shapes wants, not fundamental needs.
questions.hint: Distinguish basic needs, specific wants and wants with buying power.

options.text: Wants and demands are identical in every case
options.misconception: ignores the role of purchasing power

options.text: Needs are basic requirements, wants are specific forms shaped by culture, demands are wants with buying power
Needs are created entirely by advertising
options.misconception: confuses culturally shaped wants with basic needs

options.text: Demands come first and needs last
options.misconception: reverses the standard ordering of the concepts
